title: Largest Palindromic Number
description: You are given a string `num` consisting of digits `'0'` through `'9'`. Return the largest palindromic integer (as a string) that can be formed using any subset of digits from `num` in any order, using each digit at most as many times as it appears in `num`. The result must not have leading zeros (except for the single digit `"0"`).
hints: Greedily place pairs of the largest available digits from '9' down to '0' in the left half, skipping '0' if the left half is still empty.
Place the largest remaining unused digit (if any) in the center; if both left half and center are empty, return "0".

examples.explanation: Using pairs of '7' and '4' with '9' in the middle gives "7449447".
Only one '9' is available and leading zeros are forbidden, so "9" is optimal.
When only zeros exist, the largest valid palindromic integer is "0".
